Weather update: IMD issues red alert for Kerala and Tamil Nadu; heavy rain likely in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha
The IMD has issued red and yellow weather alerts, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, and gusty winds across southern states including Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Andhra Pradesh. Squally weather is expected over parts of the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea, prompting advis...
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on Sunday, October 25. The weather department has also forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Karnataka.
IMD has also forecast heavy rainfall over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and south interior Karnataka. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely in parts of southern India and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Heavy Rainfall warning for southern states
Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, are likely to experience heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy spells on Sunday. Heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places over Lakshadweep, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and south interior Karnataka.
The IMD has forecast thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph at isolated places in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, east Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Winds reaching 30-40 kmph are likely during thunderstorms in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep.
Weather Warning over The Bay of Bengal
Squally weather, with wind speeds of 50-60 kmph and gusts up to 70 kmph, is likely over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining west-central and southeast Bay of Bengal, as well as along and off the Andaman Islands.
Over the Arabian Sea, winds reaching 35-45 kmph, with gusts up to 55 kmph, are likely along and off the Karnataka and Kerala coasts, over the Lakshadweep region and the Comorin area.
The Met department has advised fishermen to not venture into the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal till October 26. Fishermen have also been advised to avoid the west-central and adjoining northwest and southwest Bay of Bengal from October 26 to 28, as well as waters along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts from October 27 to 28.
Extremely heavy rain in coming days
The IMD has also warned of heavy rainfall at isolated places across several southern states over the coming days, with the alert extending to parts of eastern India later.
Extremely heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe on October 26. Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are also likely to experience extremely heavy rainfall on October 27 and 28, while Telangana may see similar conditions on October 28.
Heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on October 27, as well as in Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Telangana on October 29. Very heavy rainfall is also forecast at isolated places in coastal Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe and South Interior Karnataka on October 26. The Met Office also forecast isolated very heavy spells for Odisha on October 27 and 29, along with extremely heavy rainfall on October 28.
Bihar may experience very heavy rainfall on October 30, while heavy rainfall is expected in Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim on October 29 and 30, and in Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand on October 28 and 29.
The weather department has also forecast heavy rainfall over Assam and Meghalaya on October 29 and 30, and over Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura on October 28. In north India, east Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive heavy rainfall on October 29 and 30.
